producer_statement: No single condition can be shown to explain the disagreement from the three papers alone
correction: Confirmed and stated more sharply: the only two functional comparisons (Ralvenius vs Hammer) differ at once in species (rat vs human), system (HEK293 whole-cell patch vs oocyte TEVC), agonist fraction and absolute GABA (EC10 at 1/5/8/1 uM vs EC20 at 15-60 uM), application (no preincubation, 6-10 s vs 30 s preapplication), holding potential (-60 vs -70 mV), beta isoform (beta3 for alpha2/alpha3 vs beta2 throughout), gamma2 vs gamma2S, normalisation (undefined vs EC20 = 100 percent), and laboratory. No paper varies any of these within its design (the only manipulation is Hammer gamma2S cRNA ratio at alpha2, no effect). Fisher 2011 adds a same-nominal-system (rat, HEK, patch, alpha3beta3gamma2) lab-to-lab check: diazepam efficacy 508 vs Ralvenius 227/237 percent, while diazepam EC50 agrees (59 vs 71 nM) - efficacy values differ about 2-fold between two labs in one nominal system, larger than the NDMC alpha2/alpha1 effect (1.33-1.77).

producer_statement: Which conditions confound which
correction: Not stated by producer in this form; adds: (a) species, system, patch/TEVC, preapplication and laboratory are fully collinear between Ralvenius and Hammer (one contrast, eight labels); (b) beta isoform is confounded with alpha subtype inside Ralvenius (alpha2/alpha3 beta3, alpha1 beta2; alpha5 beta2 per Methods/legend, beta3 per Table 1); (c) GABA concentration differs per subtype by design (EC10), so the agonist fraction is matched but the absolute concentration is not; (d) Emax normalisation (increment over control, probably, vs total response) differs between papers and changes the ratio (NDMC Hammer 1.33 total vs 1.65 increment).

producer_statement: Disagreement is smaller in direction than in wording
correction: Confirmed. NDMC alpha2/alpha1 is above 1 in both: Ralvenius 1.77 (printed; 1.45 if Emax were total response), Hammer 1.33 total / 1.65 increment basis, with Hammer Table 3 significant for NDMC alpha1 lower than alpha2 and alpha3 (P<0.05). Hammer non-selective is relative to clonazepam (alpha2/alpha1 1.21, alpha3/alpha1 1.51 total basis, significant for alpha3 vs alpha1), a benchmark that itself is not flat. Clobazam: Ralvenius 0.78 vs Hammer 1.02 (both at or below 1; Ralvenius has no test). Potency: both show no alpha selectivity in EC50 (Ralvenius NDMC 0.57/0.49/0.81/0.58 uM; Hammer 151/138/282/98 nM). Alpha2 and alpha3 are equal in NDMC efficacy in both papers (253 vs 245; 270 vs 270): the pattern is alpha2 = alpha3 > alpha1, so the wording alpha2-preferring is narrower than the data (alpha3 shares it), and the producer should say so.

producer_statement: NP3P3 trigger met by Ralvenius alone; two qualifications (n only a range; Emax reference undefined) right

The two qualifications are right. Add three: (i) beta isoform differs between alpha subtypes (the alpha2/alpha1 contrast is alpha2beta3 vs alpha1beta2), which fails the S0 same-subunit-composition clause for the very ratio that carries the claim; (ii) Table 1 prints alpha5beta3 while Methods and legend print alpha5beta2; (iii) no independent replication: one lab, one series, and the 2026 Phase IIa Introduction cites it alone for the alpha2 preference (the 2020 Phase I paper was seen at abstract level only). Hammer and Jensen do not meet it (diazepam only as a single 3 uM point; Jensen no efficacy and no diazepam competitor).

producer_statement: What same system requires that Ralvenius does not meet
correction: A pure alpha-subtype comparison needs the same beta (and gamma) across subtypes; Ralvenius has beta3 for alpha2 and alpha3 and beta2 for alpha1 and (Methods/legend) alpha5. Alpha2 vs alpha1 efficacy therefore mixes alpha and beta. Matched-beta pairs inside Ralvenius are alpha1 vs alpha5 (beta2) and alpha2 vs alpha3 (beta3) only. Also n per estimate is not printed, the Emax reference is not defined, and GABA is not constant across subtypes (1, 5, 8, 1 uM).
